To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified and characterized a novel enzyme IND, an indole oxygenase from Chromobacterrium violaceum, that is involved in the degradation of tryptophan to anthranilic acid, and that the enzyme is a flavoprotein.
The crystal structure of the enzyme IND, which is a flavoprotein indole oxygenase, has been solved by molecular replacement.
we have crystallized IND and determined the space group of the crystals, and that the crystals diffracted beyond 2. 1 A resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of novel, biocompatible, and biodegradable polymers and copolymers.
the study of the mechanism of the reaction catalyzed by IND.
the study of the molecular basis of the interaction of a flavoenzyme, indole oxygenase, with its substrate, indole and its reaction products, NADH and 3-hydroxyindole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystals are of the P43212 space group with a = 74.0 A and c = 152.5 A, and there is one molecule per unit cell.
the enzyme IND is a member of the family of indole oxygenases, and that it is a flavoprotein with a FAD prosthetic group.
the enzyme IND from Chromobacterum violaceum catalyses the oxidation of indole to 2-oxindole and that the reaction is coupled to the reduction of NAD+ to NADH.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have crystallized IND in the presence of NADH, a substrate analogue.
we have been able to obtain high quality diffraction data for IND in both the apo- and NADH-bound states.
IND is the first enzyme with indole 2,3-dioxygenase activity that has been crystallized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the enzyme IND, which is a flavoprotein with a redox-active FAD cofactor, catalyzes the oxidation of indole, which is an intermediate in the tryptophan degradation pathway.
the crystals diffracted to high resolution and that the enzyme is a monomer.
the enzyme has a very high degree of structural homology with the flavoprotein indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase.
